A provisional token is never inferred from activity and never a lapse claim; it is the DEFAULT the driver reads until the owner declares. An owner's declaration (packet to PROME, any token) replaces it on receipt. UNDECLARED disappears as a token for active desks.*

**Acceptance tests (written before the edit):** (1) ordinary — every active desk resolves to one token; (2) overlap — a desk with both a provisional token and a later owner declaration reads the owner's; (3) wrong owner — a retired/off-fleet name in the table is refused by `read_cadence` (the duplicate/unknown path stays); (4) missing information — a desk absent from the table still reads CANNOT-EVALUATE, never a silent WEEKLY; (5) concurrent — N/A (one writer, PROME, at closeout). **Rule letter:** *A desk whose cadence clock is PAST (WEEKLY > 7 calendar days since its last own commit; MONTHLY past the same day next month) with NO dated row naming it IS outcome ① of the dark-owner triage: PROME spawns it Tier 1 at the first boot on/after the clock runs out, as an L0 drain of its whole inbox plus a cadence self-check ("what did my domain do since my last session?"), cap = the per-boot spawn budget, beyond → slate. The exit-code contract of `spawn_list.py` is unchanged: a cadence wake is a NEW row class `CADENCE-DUE`, listed beside the dated rows, never in place of one.*
